rule: top candidates by rank: misaligned or absent litmus answer, then median under aligned, then open findings, then never used

target.target: Adapters raise typed conditions that the shared construction point renders; there is no second place a failure body is built.
target.misaligned: Each adapter builds its own body, so shapes drift, or an adapter passes an underlying library's error structure straight through to the caller.
target.evidence_expected: The single construction point for problem objects, and a search across adapters for locally constructed error responses.
target.stop: re-answered at score 2 (aligned) or better with evidence the checker verifies

target.target: The next capability call after the withdrawal fails, the unit terminates with a typed refusal naming the withdrawn identity, and the record shows who withdrew it and at which point the work stopped.
target.misaligned: Withdrawal prevents new work only, while in-flight work runs to completion under the identity that was taken away; or the work stops but nothing records why, so the stop is indistinguishable from a crash.
target.evidence_expected: A revocation performed against an agent with work in flight: the time until its next capability call fails, what the unit did between the revocation and that failure, and the record written for the stopped unit.
target.stop: re-answered at score 2 (aligned) or better with evidence the checker verifies

target.target: Suspension, resumption and forking are capability operations with a defined answer when an adapter cannot serve them, and the security boundary chosen for untrusted output is not a shared kernel.
target.misaligned: Untrusted agent output runs behind a shared-kernel boundary; or long-running work is kept alive by holding a machine idle because no suspend exists; or the core assumes one implementation's snapshot API.
target.evidence_expected: A run in which a long-running or idle unit is suspended and later resumed from saved state, or a paused sandbox is forked for parallel attempts, together with the timing and the interface signature that makes the operation optional per class.
target.stop: re-answered at score 2 (aligned) or better with evidence the checker verifies

target.target: Each mechanism is exercised on both adapters, and the effect is verified from the response - a cache hit is observed, not hoped for - with reasoning tokens counted in cost.
target.misaligned: Only plain completions are used; or directives are set in the request and never checked in the response; or cost is estimated locally from visible text, so reasoning-heavy calls are under-counted.
target.evidence_expected: For each mechanism, a request and response pair captured at the boundary showing the directive sent and the provider-reported effect returned; and for cost, a reconciliation of the build's recorded usage against the provider-reported usage fields for the same call.
target.stop: re-answered at score 2 (aligned) or better with evidence the checker verifies

target.target: A decision names the single action it admits and the moment it was taken; work resumed after a delay, a restart or a queue is decided again before its next side effect, and a rule changed in the interval takes effect on the resumed work.
target.misaligned: An allow issued at admission is carried for the life of the run; work resumed long afterwards executes under a decision made against context that no longer holds; nothing states how long a decision is good for.
target.evidence_expected: The stated scope and validity of one decision, plus a run that is admitted, delayed past that validity, and then resumed, showing whether a second evaluation happened and what input it saw.
target.stop: re-answered at score 2 (aligned) or better with evidence the checker verifies

target.target: The two counts reconcile with no unattested artifact; emission is wired where every producing path passes, so a component that attests nothing itself still yields a record; the attempt to write outside that path is refused or is structurally impossible.
target.misaligned: Coverage is asserted rather than counted; some producing paths, typically an adapter writing its own output or a step added later, leave no record; the reconciliation cannot be performed because nothing enumerates what was produced.
target.evidence_expected: A reconciliation of artifacts produced against records emitted over one period, plus the result of an attempt to produce an artifact through a component that carries no attestation code of its own.
target.stop: re-answered at score 2 (aligned) or better with evidence the checker verifies

target.target: Every mechanism is present and verified from the exchange itself, including the resource indicator on refresh, and tool results are validated against declared output schemas rather than read as prose.
target.misaligned: The deprecated event-stream transport is in use; authorization is a shared secret or a bearer token with no audience binding; the resource indicator is present on issue but dropped on refresh; results are parsed out of free text.
target.evidence_expected: A captured authorization exchange for one remote surface including the refresh, showing the resource indicator present in both; and the transport actually negotiated.
target.stop: re-answered at score 2 (aligned) or better with evidence the checker verifies
